_what_this_is: THE STACK-SPECIFIC HALF OF THE HARNESS, in one file.
`ci.py` is the step ladder: run each rung in order, print a positive marker with
a count, name the rung that stopped the run. That part IS the same in every
factory. What is NOT the same is every command it runs, so the commands live
here instead of in the ladder.
Set what you have. Leave a step empty and it is SKIPPED LOUDLY -- the log says
<STEP>_SKIPPED and the gate can be told to require the marker, so a skipped rung
is never mistaken for a passed one.
_unit_count_pattern: A regex with ONE group capturing how many tests ran. ZERO IS NOT A PASS: a suite that discovered nothing exits 0 and looks perfect. Leave empty to skip the count check, and accept that you cannot tell a passing suite from an absent one.
_driver: How the E2E reaches your software. THREE SHAPES cover almost everything:
http     a server. Started on a dynamic port, polled until healthy.
cli      a command. Invoked with args, stdout/stderr asserted.
library  no process at all. The E2E imports and calls it.
A frontend app is `http` plus a browser-automation CLI in your e2e.py. A
rendered window or a game loop is NONE of these -- the logic has to live behind
a headless surface an E2E can drive, and that is an architecture decision to
make before the code exists, not after.

http._env: Optional extra environment for the app process. {port} is substituted.

cli._note: The command under test. {args} is substituted per call from e2e.py.

library._note: Nothing to start. APP_STARTED is emitted after this import succeeds, which is the equivalent proof that the thing loads at all.

browser._note: ONLY for an app whose correctness is visual. Leave install_check empty if e2e.py never drives a browser. When it is set, `darkfactory doctor` runs it at setup -- so a missing browser is a setup failure with an install command, not a mystery hang at gate time on a fresh runner.
browser.install_hint: npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install   |   pip install playwright && playwright install chromium
